newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy confirms monetary policy aimed at CPI.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy confirms monetary policy aimed at CPI.

text.p: The Bank of Italy's monetary policy remains aimed at reducing inflation to the level seen in other major industrialised countries, central bank governor Antonio Fazio said in a speech on Wednesday.

"Monetary policy has drastically reduced inflationary expectations and inflation. It remains firmly oriented to keeping inflation in line with that observed in the other leading industrial countries," Fazio said.
He added that inflation would have to be kept "firmly below three percent" in 1997.
Italian inflation in October was three percent. The government has set an inflation target for next year of an average 2.5 percent.
Fazio told a conference organised by Euromoney that Italy was laying the foundations for a new phase of growth within a framework of European integration.

"The macroeconomic conditions exist for further expansion of the financial markets. On the supply side there is the high saving rate of Italian households. On the demand side there are numerous profitable and efficient firms with excellent growth prospects," Fazio said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
